card.name: Linking words before patient risk factors
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as a, an, or, have, higher or either that come right before a patient risk factor or baseline condition, in phrases like "patients with" or "have". Also fires on the T of TIA.

modes.label: Articles after 'patients with'
modes.description: A or an right after "patients with" or "have", before a history or lab value.
modes.example: The risk of amputation was highest in patients with<< a>> baseline history of diabetic foot, peripheral artery

modes.label: Risk-factor list items
modes.description: Words that open the next item in a list of patient traits or conditions.
modes.example: Patients with amputations were more likely to be male, have<< higher>> A1C (%) at baseline, have

modes.label: Inside condition names
modes.description: Start of an abbreviated condition name after stroke or.
modes.example: A higher incidence of hemorrhagic stroke was seen in patients without CHD but with stroke or<< T>>IA within the previous 6 months in

card.writes: It suppresses outcome words, so the next word is more likely a condition or finding than the word outcome.
card.plain: It fires on small words that introduce a patient's risk factor or baseline condition, such as history or lab value.
